chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Ibn Abi Umayr from Muawiya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the one who is overcome by nausea (but does not vomit) while fasting, he said: Let him complete his fast and he does not have to make it up.

key_terms.وَلَا يَقْضِي: and he does not make it up (qada)
key_terms.يَذْرَعُهُ: to be overcome by or to be afflicted with (nausea)

ai.seo_question: Does nausea without vomiting break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this ruling from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the sensation of nausea and the actual expulsion of vomit, establishing that mere nausea does not break the fast. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that involuntary bodily sensations do not invalidate worship unless they result in the physical release of material, ensuring believers are not burdened by uncertainty during their fasts.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin ShAzan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the one who nauseates to vomit (but does not), and he is Fasting. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Let him complete his Fast and the does not have to make up for it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from ibn abu ‘Umayr, from Mu‘awiyah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who feels like vomiting must complete his fast and there is no Qada’ (compensatory fast) on him.’”
